impact: The plan explicitly allows the low-level NETWORK adapter to inspect native error codes, conflicting with the hard constraint that only the FS adapter may inspect a native error; branding the outcome prevents core logic from inspecting it but does not satisfy the restriction on where the original native error is inspected. NOT IMPLEMENTED under the unchanged constraint — flagged for an explicit owner amendment and recorded in section 12, because this is a constraint question rather than a design choice I can settle. It genuinely blocks something real rather than being a wording quibble: the port lock must distinguish EADDRINUSE from EACCES or a sandbox refusal, and T-008 is explicit that collapsing those is the indeterminate-becomes-an-answer defect. Two coherent resolutions, both the owner's: widen the constraint to 'a designated low-level adapter' naming the net adapter alongside the fs one, or route net failures through the single authorized adapter.
resolution:
RESOLVED by N-007 decision 3, verified against .story/notes/N-007.json on 2026-08-04.

The issue was filed because the T-011 plan let a low-level NETWORK adapter inspect native errors while the standing constraint said only the FS adapter may. N-007 #3 already settled it, verbatim:

  "native errors are inspected only at an adapter; fs was simply the only adapter that existed. ADD A NETWORK ADAPTER owning EADDRINUSE/EACCES classification exactly as the fs adapter owns fs errnos. The constraint generalizes; it does not bend."

So the constraint was never "only the fs adapter" as a principle — fs was simply the only adapter in existence when it was written. The generalized form is "native errors are inspected only at AN adapter, and each adapter owns its own errnos". A network adapter owning EADDRINUSE/EACCES satisfies it rather than violating it.

Found while assessing T-011 plan review round 1 (codex session 019fcee9), which raised the conflict as a finding. I verified it before treating it as a blocker, and the verification is what showed it is already decided — so it is NOT a T-011 park reason. The remaining obligation is on the plan, not on this issue: cite N-007 #3 and carry the generalized wording, so the next reader does not re-derive the conflict from the older phrasing.

Worth recording for anyone carrying the constraint list forward: the phrasing "only the fs adapter may inspect a native error" is the PRE-N-007 wording and is now misleading. The current wording is "native errors are inspected only at an adapter, which owns its own errnos".
title: [constraint-violation] The plan explicitly allows the low-level NETWORK adapter to inspect native error
